articles.title: Brain imaging study links childhood trauma to chronic procrastination in adulthood
articles.summary: Childhood trauma can leave a lasting mark on brain development. A new study reveals how these early neurobiological changes elevate anxiety and reduce self-control, paving the way for chronic procrastination in adulthood.

articles.title: Flow-by-Flow:Content-Judgment Bypass for Governing AI Output in High-Loss Domains
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07474v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Prior work showed that human-in-the-loop oversight becomes structurally untenable in high-loss domains when AI output velocity V exceeds human cognitive capacity C_max. The operative constraint, however, is not V alone but V x L, where L denotes per-item cognitive load. L consists of triage, judgment, and response, which respond asymmetrically to AI capability improvement. Triage cost does not decline as models become more capable, because semantic indeterminacy is inherent in general-purpose design. Response cost is invariant to accuracy improve

articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07476v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a formal framework for constructing canonical interpretations from plural structure theories. A structure theory is a triple T = ({\Sigma}, A, I) consisting of a signature, axioms, and an inference policy, whose admissible interpretation family collects all globally consistent assignments of structural conclusions. articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Active inference has emerged as a principled framework for modeling adaptive behavior by balancing goal-directed action with uncertainty reduction. The present work focuses on machine learning algorithms as a tool well suited for analyzing and recognizing online banking transactions. articles.title: Teen cannabis use linked to slower memory and thinking growth
articles.summary: Teens who start using cannabis may experience slower growth in memory, attention, language, and processing speed. Their abilities often developed normally at first, then began leveling off while nonusers continued improving. THC appeared to be the most likely driver, especially for worsening memory.

articles.title: A surprising shift in sniffing and odor perception could be a key sign of Parkinson’s disease
articles.summary: A novel test measuring how people describe and physically sniff odors can accurately distinguish Parkinson's disease from other causes of smell loss. The findings suggest the disease alters sensory processing rather than just dulling the senses.

articles.title: Evolving Safety Landscape of Multi-modal Large Language Models: A Survey of Emerging Threats and Safeguards
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07535v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-modal large language models (MLLMs) integrate heterogeneous modalities through modality alignment and fusion, enabling stronger understanding and reasoning. However, this architectural shift reshapes the safety landscape of machine learning. Increased model complexity and cross-modal interactions give rise to novel threats, including compromised modality integration, modality misalignment, and fused safety risks, reflecting shifts in threat modeling beyond uni-modal assumptions. articles.title: Tracing sources of epistemic uncertainty in deep learning predictions: homo- and hetero-scedastic linearized estimators
articles.summary: arXiv:2608.07630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We adapt two classical statistical estimators for quantifying uncertainty to modern deep learning, in order to provide clearer insights into uncertainty attributable to two sources : aleatoric uncertainty, or locally scarce data. Our approach leverages recent advances in approximate Fisher Information Matrices, to enable scaling to actual architectures. articles.title: Narcissism and psychopathy linked to entrepreneurial mindsets
articles.summary: Individuals who score higher in dark personality traits like narcissism and psychopathy also report a stronger internal drive to start their own businesses. The findings suggest that socially undesirable traits provide unique insights into entrepreneurial behavior.

articles.title: Confidence is detection-like in high-dimensional spaces
articles.summary: arXiv:2410.18933v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Confidence estimates are often "detection-like" - driven by positive evidence in favour of a decision. This empirical observation has been interpreted as showing that human metacognition is limited by biases or heuristics. Here, we show that Bayesian confidence estimates also exhibit heightened sensitivity to decision-congruent evidence in higher-dimensional signal detection theoretic spaces, leading to detection-like confidence criteria. articles.title: Believing the world is unfair may explain why some who experience adversity are drawn to conspiracy theories
articles.summary: New research published in the British Journal of Psychology suggests that experiencing personal hardship does not directly cause conspiracy beliefs. Instead, adversity tends to foster a sense of injustice, which then makes conspiratorial ideas more appealing.

articles.title: Social isolation harms the aging brain independently of loneliness
articles.summary: New research reveals that physical social isolation harms the aging brain independently of subjective feelings of loneliness. Simulated public health interventions show that reconnecting isolated older adults can directly protect against cognitive decline.

articles.title: Study links short-form video addiction to a decline in teenagers’ academic coping skills
articles.summary: A one-year study tracking high school students suggests addictive use of short-form videos limits teenagers' ability to focus on the future. This shortened perspective makes it harder for them to bounce back from everyday academic setbacks.
